mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 2.0% consistently reduces equity discount rates and stimulates corporate borrowing, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without regime dependence.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS remains below 2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 4.0% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions that suppress consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 4.0% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous 3% month-over-month declines in retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate broad consumer demand contraction that triggers equity sell-offs, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in RSAFS and HOUST fails to predict negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances (Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production declining more than 5% month-over-month during supply chain disruptions signals manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate margins, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO declines exceed 5% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: Year-over-year CPI inflation exceeding 3.0% triggers Fed tightening expectations that increase equity discount rates, generating negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL YoY exceeds 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Non-farm payroll growth exceeding 150,000 jobs monthly indicates robust labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS growth exceeds 150,000 jobs.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth exceeding 2.5% annualized in late-cycle expansions signals demand saturation that reduces corporate profit growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.5% annualized.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production falling below 100 (index base 2017=100) indicates imminent recessionary supply contraction that depresses equity valuations, generating negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO falls below 100.
